common_rust.title: Possible common maize rust
common_rust.confirm: Look for raised reddish-brown pustules on maize leaves. Inspect both sides and check other plants.
precautions: Photograph multiple leaves and document how widespread symptoms are.
Seek local extension advice if symptoms are widespread or progressing.
prevention: Ask local extension services about resistant maize varieties adapted to the area.
Monitor crops regularly and record when symptoms first appear.
common_rust.limitations: Leaf discoloration alone cannot confirm common rust.

gray_leaf_spot.title: Possible gray leaf spot
gray_leaf_spot.confirm: Look for tan-gray, often rectangular lesions that run parallel to veins; older symptoms may merge.
precautions: Inspect multiple plants and note whether lower leaves are affected.
Consult an extension officer when damage is extensive or the pattern is uncertain.
prevention: Discuss locally adapted resistant varieties with an extension officer.
Consider crop rotation with non-host crops when planning future seasons, considering local agronomic conditions.
gray_leaf_spot.limitations: Early lesions overlap with other foliar diseases; symptoms alone are insufficient.

northern_leaf_blight.title: Possible northern / Turcicum leaf blight
northern_leaf_blight.confirm: Look for long, expanding tan lesions and substantial damaged leaf areas, especially in humid conditions.
precautions: Inspect additional plants and record growth stage and symptom spread.
Seek extension review if a large leaf area is affected.
prevention: Discuss resistant maize cultivars suitable for local conditions.
Review rotation and crop-residue practices with agricultural extension staff.
northern_leaf_blight.limitations: Severe lesions can resemble other disease and noninfectious injury.

healthy.title: No supported disease pattern recognized
healthy.confirm: The model only compares the photo against its four training classes; it cannot establish that a plant is free of disease.
precautions: If the plant is still showing unusual symptoms, take additional photos and seek extension advice.
prevention: Inspect plants regularly and use locally recommended crop-health practices.
healthy.limitations: A healthy class prediction does not rule out pests, viruses, nutrient deficiencies or drought stress.
